To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
rat androgen-binding-protein and human sex-steroid-binding-protein bind specifically to rat spermatogenic cells.
a plasma membrane receptor for rABP and a plasma membrane receptor with high affinity binding for hSBP were identified in isolated adult male rat germ cells.
the receptor binding sites of rat androgen-binding proteins and human sex hormone-binding protein are identical.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a receptor for the rat androgen-binding proteins (rABP), a protein complex of 100-120 kDa which is present in the cytosol of the adult rat germ cells.
the identification and characterization of a receptor for rABP in the germ cells of the rat.
the identification of specific binding sites in the plasma membranes of isolated adult rat germ cell populations and the characterization of the nature of the binding proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
rABP and/or hSBP are involved in the regulation of spermatogenesis.

the receptor binding of rABP and/or hSBP in the plasma membrane of adult rat germ cells is pH dependent, and is specific for both androgen-binding carrier molecules, and that this binding is abolished by EDTA.
rABP and its human analogue, hSBP, have a common receptor in the plasma membrane of adult rat germ cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rABP receptor is present on germ cells in the testis and is also present in the plasma membrane-enriches fractions of germ cells.
rABP binds specifically to a receptor on rat germ cells.
rABP binds to the germ cell plasma membrane receptor and is internalized into the germ cell cytoplasm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the plasma membrane receptor for rABP and for hSBP is the same.
the receptor for ABP and SBP is present in the plasma membranes of germ cells and that it is capable of forming a complex with these carrier proteins.
we have developed a novel method of isolating and characterizing the plasma membrane of the rat germ cell.
